title: PCR nose and throat swab
what: A nurse gently runs a soft swab in your nose and throat and sends it to the lab. The test looks for traces of viruses or bacteria.
why: For a cold, cough, or fever, and when it is required for travel, work, or a hospital stay.
duration: the swab itself takes about a minute, and results usually take 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: If you often get nosebleeds, or had surgery on your nose
If you have a strong gag reflex

prepare.title: 3 to 4 hours before
prepare.text: Usually do not eat, drink, brush your teeth, gargle, or chew gum. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Nose
prepare.text: On the day of the test, do not use nose drops or sprays, and do not rinse your nose, unless your doctor said otherwise.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Do not smoke for a few hours before the swab.

bring: A face mask, if you have cold symptoms
steps: You sit down and tilt your head back a little
The swab goes into your nostril and is turned for a few seconds
Then you open your mouth, and the swab is run along the back of your throat
The swabs go into a tube and are labeled
feel: In the nose: a tickle. You may want to sneeze, and your eyes may water
In the throat: you may gag for a second
after: The discomfort passes in a few minutes
While you wait for the result, if you have a cold, try to keep away from other people
red_flags: A nosebleed that does not stop in 15 to 20 minutes: see a doctor or call emergency services

faq.a: It does not hurt, but it is unpleasant. It tickles and you may want to sneeze. It lasts a few seconds.

faq.q: Can I eat before a PCR swab?
faq.a: It is best not to eat or drink for 3 to 4 hours. Otherwise the swab may not collect enough material.

reminders.text: PCR swab in a few hours. From now on, do not eat, drink, brush your teeth, or use nose drops.
